newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to meet UN's Annan Jan. 23.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to meet UN's Annan Jan. 23.

text.p: President Bill Clinton will meet new U.N. Secretary General Kofi Annan on Jan. 23, their first meeting since the Ghanaian became head of the world body, the White House said on Wednesday.

The United States was the moving force in ousting Annan's predecessor, Boutros Boutros-Ghali, arguing that the Egyptian had not moved forcefully enough to reform the United Nations. A U.S. official said the issue of reform, as well as the related matter of the $1.3 billion the United States owes the United Nations, were expected to come up during the meeting.

"Mostly, this is an opportunity for the president to welcome Mr. Annan for the first time after his selection as secretary general," he said. "He is looking foward to having a very strong discussion with him about how to reform the U.N."

The official said Clinton wanted to meet Annan early in his term, adding that the timing was decided in part to ensure Annan would visit Washington while Congress was in session so he could meet U.S. legislators.

Congressional Republicans have attacked the United Nations as bloated, inefficient and wasteful and have balked at paying off the U.S. debt to the institution until it is reformed. The $1.3 billion the United States owes is more than half the $2.3 billion owed to the world body by its members.
At the United Nations in New York, Annan told reporters he was not bringing any specific issues to the meeting but would make the the case to U.S. officials "that we all need the United Nations."
